title: The claim to square with predestination too
source_text: CXXXIX. Denique gloriantur qui sunt in hac opinione, gratiae efficaciam sic a se expositam, non solum cum arbitrii humani libertate, optime consistere; sed etiam cum certitudine divinae praedestinationis. Quandoquidem secundum illam, praedestinatio habet suum effectum, per auxilia quidem in se repudiabilia; ita tamen genio voluntatis accommodata, ut juxta praescientiam Dei, effectum infallibiliter sint habitura.
pass_a_gloss: CXXXIX. Finally those who are of this opinion boast that the efficacy of grace thus set forth by them, agrees excellently not only with the freedom of human choice; but also with the certainty of divine predestination. Since according to it, predestination has its effect, through aids indeed in themselves rejectable; yet so adjusted to the temper of the will, that according to the foreknowledge of God, they will infallibly have effect.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXXXIX. Lastly, those who hold this opinion pride themselves that the efficacy of grace, as they explain it, fits perfectly not only with the freedom of human choice but also with the certainty of divine predestination. On this view predestination achieves its effect through aids that can in themselves be rejected, yet are so suited to the will's temper that, in line with God's foreknowledge, they will take effect infallibly.
